Subject: Follow-up from today — tokens, budget, SLOs

Marissa — thanks for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can move toward a pilot: 

- Rough monthly token volume: 4–8M tokens/month for initial pilot, with peak bursts up to ~1.2M tokens/day.
- Target budget for pilot: ~$3k–$8k/month (flexible if performance warrants).
- Critical SLO for user flows: 95th pct latency under 600ms for single-turn text completion (user-facing search/autocomplete), and streaming enabled for conversational flows.

Can you confirm an expected $/1M tokens for the different latency tiers you discussed (hosted standard, hosted fast, dedicated burst)? Also interested in batching/streaming tradeoffs — if we prioritize 95th<600ms, what's the expected price delta vs a cost-optimized config?

Appreciate a simple table if possible. Happy to jump on a quick follow-up with your SEs.

Thanks,
Alex
CTO, FintechAI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — tokens, budget, SLOs

Alex — great to connect earlier. Below is a quick, pragmatic breakdown to help you weigh latency vs cost. Attaching our throughput benchmark CSV and a draft SOW with pilot milestones.

High-level pricing (examples, final quote depends on sustained throughput and contract term):
- Hosted Standard (cost-optimized): ~$250 / 1M tokens — typical for batched, non-streaming workloads with relaxed p95.
- Hosted Fast (low-latency tier): ~$1,000 / 1M tokens — reserved for lower-latency, smaller batch sizes and streaming enablement.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): starting at $7,500/mo reserved + ~$500 / 1M tokens for overage — predictable latency/SLA at higher sustained throughput.

Latency vs cost notes:
- Streaming enabled + low-batch sizing reduces p95 by ~2–3x vs heavy batching but increases per-token execution cost (compute inefficiency).
- Autoscaling/dedicated capacity reduces unit cost at scale (we amortize GPU time) and gives consistent p95.
- For your pilot (4–8M/mo) we often recommend Hosted Fast for the initial iteration if p95 < 600ms is critical; it keeps up-front commits low while meeting SLOs. If you quickly ramp, move to Dedicated for better $/1M.

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi to share a simple unit-economics table with example batching/streaming configs and expected $/1M at 4M and 8M tokens.
2) If those look good, we'll send a 30-day pilot SOW + access details.
3) Quick technical sync with your infra team to confirm network egress and token accounting.

Attachments: throughput-benchmarks.csv, SOW-draft.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Hi Alex — following up with the technical split you asked for. Below are realistic, example configs and expected unit economics. These are illustrative; we'll run a short benchmark on your sample prompts during the pilot to nail numbers.

Config A — Cost-optimized (Hosted Standard)
- Batch size: 16–32 requests per GPU step; streaming: off
- Expected p95 (single-turn): 1.0–1.5s
- Estimated cost: ~$250 / 1M tokens
- Best for: high throughput background tasks or non-interactive enrichment.

Config B — Balanced (Hosted Fast)
- Batch size: 4–8; streaming: on for conversational flows; KV-prefetch enabled
- Expected p95: ~350–700ms (depends on prompt size and model)
- Estimated cost: ~$700–$1,000 / 1M tokens (we quoted $1,000 above as upper bound)
- Best for: user-facing flows where p95 matters but you want to avoid dedicated commitments.

Config C — Dedicated reserved
- Dedicated GPU pool, small batch sizes, streaming enabled, priority kernel paths
- Expected p95: ~200–400ms consistently
- Cost math (example): $7,500/mo reserved baseline + ~$500 / 1M tokens for incremental usage
- Best for: consistent heavy traffic where predictable latency and lower marginal cost needed.

Notes on sizing and burst behavior:
- Bursts: for short spikes we recommend burstable capacity (available on Dedicated) or configured fallback to a slightly higher-latency model variant to preserve availability.
- Token accounting: we will provide per-call token breakdowns and a dashboard so you can map feature-level unit economics.

Quick unit-economics table (rounded):
- 4M tokens/mo: Hosted Standard ~$1k/mo; Hosted Fast ~$2.8k–4k/mo; Dedicated baseline ~$7.5k + (4M * $0.0005) ~= $9.5k/mo
- 8M tokens/mo: Hosted Standard ~$2k/mo; Hosted Fast ~$5.6k–8k/mo; Dedicated baseline ~$7.5k + (8M * $0.0005) ~= $11.5k/mo

I'll also run a short bench against your sample prompts — Marissa, can you share the sample prompt set and a small dataset (50–100 prompts)? Alex, if you can drop that on the Drive link Marissa included, we'll run it and return measured p95 and cost estimates.

Cheers,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
